sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 22nd ed. Dallas: SIL. Entry 'Mukha-Dora [mmk]' (Wayback snapshot of 2019-05-12).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'Classification: Dravidian, South-Central, Gondi-Kui, Konda-Kui, Konda. Language Use: Use Telugu [tel] as L1 (Singh 1994b). Also use Adivasi Oriya [ort].' Alternate names Conta-Reddi, Mukha Dhora, Nooka Dora, Nuka-Dora, Reddi, Reddi-Dora, Riddi.

sources.citation: Team of TCR&TI and TCR&TM, Andhra Pradesh. 2018. Basic Statistics and Brief Ethnographic Profile of Tribes of Andhra Pradesh. Dept. of Tribal Welfare, Govt of Andhra Pradesh. Sections 'Mooka Dora / Nooka Dora' (PDF leaf 21) and 'Reddy Dora' (PDF leaf 24).
sources.note: Nothing on stress or on any linguistic feature; states 'Their mother tongue is Telugu but they also speak Adivasi Oriya' (Mooka/Nooka Dora section) and 'The Mukhadoras, who are also known as Nookadoras... They speak Telugu' (Reddy Dora section).

sources.citation: Omniglot, 'Mukha Dora script' page (Prasanna Sree's constructed script); Wikipedia 'Mukha-Dora language' (stub citing Ethnologue 18 and Zvelebil 1990).

sources.citation: von Fürer-Haimendorf, Christoph. 1945. The Reddis of the Bison Hills: A study in acculturation. London: Macmillan (Glottolog ref 96716, the only 'descriptive' ref Glottolog lists). scanned text of the Digital Library of India scan.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; ethnography of the Konda Reddis. Introduction (scan leaf 24): 'While the Koyas in these parts speak a dialect of Gondi, the Reddis have no other language than Telugu'; social-organization chapter (printed p. 65): clan names 'are relics of a language spoken by the Reddis before they adopted Telugu'. No word 'Mukha' or 'Nuka Dora' occurs in the scanned text.
